svg.title: The Live-Trading Latency Ladder
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-live-trading-latency-ladder; chapter number: 2; title: The Live-Trading Latency Ladder; subtitle: Seconds separating consumer signals from the traders already moving the price; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: seconds; bars: label: OddsJam odds refresh; min: 5; max: 5; typical: 5; display: 5 seconds; label: ESPN Gamecast lead over TV; min: 5; max: 15; typical: 10; display: 5 to 15 seconds; label: Consumer stream delay; min: 7; max: 30; typical: 10; display: 7, 10 or up to 30 seconds; label: Free feed lag; min: 15; max: 30; typical: 22.5; display: 15 to 30 seconds; label: Dashboard cache window; min: 30; max: 30; typical: 30; display: 30 seconds; caption: Latency is the hard ceiling on live cross-venue trading: an ESPN-fed Kalshi bot lost money as Kalshi moved before the free signal, while pro feeds run near $5,000 a month.; assumptions note: Typical values are the midpoint of the stated range where no point estimate was given (Gamecast, free feed); the consumer stream typical uses the 10-second figure named by the speaker. Refresh and cache bars come from odds-API practitioners for comparison.; note: Attributed to Part Time Larry (bA_NUrMJuw4), Whale Slots (QpjzafRRmjQ), OddsJam (ZTKIge6SyQI) and SportsGameOdds API (JXdlRbDVFNY).
